r: Your deck hides its most important number. The 40% month-over-month revenue growth only appears on slide nine, after three slides of market-sizing boilerplate. Investors decide quickly on a seed pitch. According to DocSend's averages, they often spend under 4 minutes on the whole deck, and they form a view within the first 3 minutes. That means your traction metric, the one number your fundraising argument depends on, shows up after their attention has gone. Your opening slide also leads with a mission statement when the data should come first. Move growth to slide two, then give the customer acquisition cost payback period of 5 months, then explain the problem. Right now the deck reads like a slow mystery novel, and readers skip to the end or quit. Investors may also assume the delay was deliberate. Cut the market-sizing preamble to one line and let traction speak.
